thread:
sara-platform: heads up — noticed a spike of enforcement rejections that don't show up in metering for ~30s windows for some orgs. looks like enforcement reads from cached credits and metering stream is lagging behind by 20–40s.

mike-infra: ugh. which cache? the per-key credit cache on enforcer?

sara-platform: yes, the in-memory burst cache on enforcer nodes. eviction/refresh happens async from the ingestion pipeline. when stream lag > refresh interval, enforcer thinks credits exhausted and rejects even though downstream metering will later credit the org.

jordan-eng: can you paste a log example?

sara-platform: sure — obf logs below (redacted):
```
2026-03-18T15:02:11Z enforcer[pid:42] WARN key=org_1234 reason=reject token_bucket.remain=0 cache_age=36s metering_lag_est=28s
2026-03-18T15:02:12Z metering-consumer[pid:9] INFO org=org_1234 events_ingested=120 window_start=15:01:30
```

karen-sre: that cache_age and lag lines up. probable root cause: kafka consumer lag on the metering pipeline in eu-west region — saw a partition leader flapped yesterday.

mike-infra: short-term mitigation: increase local grace window on enforcer from 10s to 60s and serve a permissive fallback when metering lag detected. long-term: reconcile model so enforcement trusts durable store, not just memory.

jordan-eng: agree. but raising grace window risks letting real overuse through. propose: for orgs with high historical burst tolerance, use permissive mode; for others, use a tiered approach. We can gate by feature flag.

sara-platform: thinking rollout plan: 1) enable permissive fallback behind FF for 5% of orgs (canary) 2) monitor fraud/overuse signals for 2h 3) expand to 25% 4) snapshot and run reconciliation backfill to ensure ledger catches up 5) revert FF.

ops-bot: ALERT: metering-pipeline consumer lag > 2m in eu-west (partitions: 6/24), incident created #inc-4287

karen-sre: since incident exists, we should also rate-limit enforcement retries to avoid thundering replays. enforcement should return 429 with Retry-After when in permissive fallback to avoid client hammering.

mike-infra: implementation notes:
- add metric enforcer.cache_miss_lag_seconds
- add boolean enforcer.permissive_mode_via_ff(org_id)
- when permissive_mode true and cache_age > threshold => allow and annotate response header `X-Rate-Decision:permissive-cache`

jordan-eng: for reconciliation backfill: read raw ingest events from S3/segment store, aggregate per org, compute delta between committed ledger and derived usage, write idempotent ledger adjustments to enforcement store with op_id = sha256(ingest_file + offset). ensure CAS to avoid races.

sara-platform: important: avoid double-counting. backfill must only apply when ingestion timestamp < reconciliation_cutoff and not previously applied. include last_applied_offset per partition in ledger.

support-sig: from support side — if we flip permissive for canary, we need an inbox template explaining possible delayed billing and transient 429s during rollback. also add a dashboard note so CS sees which orgs are in canary.

mike-infra: dashboard items to add now:
- enforcement_rejections_per_min by org (heatmap)
- metering_consumer_lag_seconds by partition/region
- percent_orgs_with_cache_age_gt_threshold
- canary_org_list tag on traces

jordan-eng: alerting thresholds: metering_consumer_lag_seconds > 45s for >5m => P1; percent_orgs_with_rejections > 0.5% => P2.

sara-platform: deployment plan: small FF rollout today (5% canary) at 16:30 UTC. monitor 0–30m for false negatives on throttles and 30–120m for cost exposure. rollback window = 2h by default.

karen-sre: add circuit-breaker: if support reports >10 orgs complaining in canary or if billing delta > $X/hour, auto-revert FF.

mike-infra: quick toggle command for oncall:
```bash
# enable permissive for canary flag key=burst.permissive_canary
curl -XPOST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" https://console.internal/features/burst.permissive_canary/toggle -d '{"percent":5}'
```

sara-platform: i'll create the playbook and the dashboard tiles now. Jordan/mike — can you pair on backfill job idempotency? prefer to land tests tomorrow morning.

jordan-eng: on it. I'll add unit tests for op_id collisions and a dry-run mode that emits a reconciliation plan without writing.

support-sig: tagging CS on rollout PR and will prep the canned responses.

sara-platform: thanks. action items summarized: (1) FF canary 5% today 16:30 UTC (mike) (2) dashboard + alerts (mike) (3) backfill design + tests (jordan) (4) playbook & support template (support-sig) (5) circuit-breaker for auto-revert (karen).

mike-infra: acked. will post runbook link once FF is queued.

deploy-bot: deployment queued: feature/burst-permissive-flag -> canary(5%) by mike-infra at 2026-03-18T16:29:00Z

sara-platform: :thumbsup: will follow up after 1h for initial metrics.
